# Independent prompt-first usability execution

Reviewer: independent_review. These answers were written before reading fixture assertions, fixture README/index grading, implementation tests, or upstream source. Inputs were only user_request.txt and the installed-style PyTorch/TorchNPU root skills, eight sub-skills each, and their workflow references. Selected one synthetic prompt for each sub-skill plus the root and both integrated prompts: 22 cases. This is a textual execution of the procedures, not an accelerator, compiler, distributed, model-quality or service measurement. No backend execution is claimed. All proposed checks below remain not run by this reviewer unless separately stated in the review record.

## pytorch/root/backend-snapshot-routing

Start with the PyTorch root inspector, recording installed torch version/build identity separately from the pinned 2.16.0a0 source, Python/OS, wheel backend, available device/runtime, workload shapes/dtypes/strides, grad mode, state/seed, batch and timing boundary. A newer independent TorchNPU checkout establishes no compatibility pairing. Route stack selection to installation-and-build; establish eager correctness and a bounded profile through profiling-and-debugging. Then route guard/capture issues to compiler-and-export, loading/pinning to training-and-data plus memory-streams-and-graphs, and multi-rank/state to distributed-and-checkpoint. Before compilation compare eager outputs and gradients and distinguish capture, lowering, cold compile and steady state. Before pinned loaders prove sample correctness, source-buffer lifetime, transfer order and full input-pipeline/host-memory cost. Before distributed training qualify backend/rank/device mapping, matching collective sequences and state/data partitions. CPU controls do not qualify CUDA/NPU or multi-rank execution; unavailable checks remain BLOCKED_REQUIRED_BACKEND, efficacy not_run.

## pytorch/sub-skills/installation-and-build/wheel-versus-source-build

Preserve the current environment. Create a separate supported Python >=3.11 environment and a trusted source checkout at the selected revision, with recursive submodules; an inspection-only shallow checkout cannot build. Record compiler/ABI, Windows Visual Studio C++20 tools, Ninja/CMake, resources and selected CUDA toolkit, compatible host compiler and cuDNN. This pin uses scikit-build-core, not the obsolete setup.py build recipe; install declared build requirements before `python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -v -e .`. Configure only required backends and conservative MAX_JOBS. BUILD_/USE_/CMAKE_ variables plus declared aliases are forwarded; use `-Ccmake.define.<OPTION>=<VALUE>` for supported nonforwarded options. CMAKE_ONLY/CMAKE_FRESH/USE_NINJA are removed. Active Windows pyproject uses Ninja/cl and takes precedence over stale README generator guidance. Verify from outside the source tree, recording actual installed git version. Run CPU smoke and tiny synchronized device allocation/op on the intended CUDA build, followed by extension compile/link/import, registration and numerical/gradient/stream checks. The existing CPU wheel plus a toolkit proves neither CUDA wheel capability nor extension correctness; build/device execution is not performed here.

## pytorch/sub-skills/tensor-dispatch-autograd/detached-alias-and-jagged-offsets

Inspect shape/stride/storage offset, dtype/device/layout, requires_grad, leaf and grad_fn and identify storage aliases. detach removes history but shares storage; mutating the detached view can change the saved value/version and invalidate backward. Remove or postpone mutation until backward completes, or make independent storage with clone when isolation is intended; retain gradient history if the clone must be differentiable. Do not use .data or disable autograd to hide the problem. Run a tiny value/gradient comparison. For the jagged error, equal lengths do not necessarily imply the same ragged symbol: rebuild related tensors using the same offsets constituent when their structure is truly shared. Check constructor/history and exact operator support; if unsupported, only use padded dense plus masking after verifying semantics and memory. Blanket contiguous conversion does not solve either ownership contract.

## pytorch/sub-skills/training-and-data/amp-loader-attention-interaction

Begin with num_workers=0, prefetch_factor=None and persistent_workers=False and a small in-memory dataset with sample IDs. Verify one sample/batch and complete epoch uniqueness/count. Implement IterableDataset sharding across worker AND distributed rank; on Windows keep launch under a main guard and worker/collate functions top-level picklable. Add four workers only after correctness, seed their RNGs and reset persistent dataset state explicitly per epoch. Accumulate loss normalized by the actual number of microbatches, hold one scale throughout the window, then unscale once, clip unscaled gradients, scaler.step and scaler.update once per effective optimizer update. Keep backward outside autocast and record skipped updates. Set SDPA dropout_p=0.0 explicitly for evaluation; eval() does not change a passed functional dropout value. Preserve masks (SDPA boolean True attends), causal/head/layout contracts. Run the bundled tiny_training.py --steps 2 as a no-download CPU state/update control and a tiny sample-ID check at 0 then 4 workers; separately qualify accelerator AMP/SDPA. A finite CPU loss is no convergence or device proof.

## pytorch/sub-skills/compiler-and-export/recompilation-and-export-range

Retain the eager control and compare exact initial state, outputs and gradients. Use backend=eager, then aot_eager, then actual Inductor/target to isolate Dynamo, AOTAutograd and lowering/runtime. Inspect TORCH_LOGS=graph_breaks,recompiles,guards: changing batch and Python scalar guards can invalidate cached variants, whereas graph breaks segment capture. dynamic=True attempts dynamic kernels but does not eliminate scalar/object guards or all specialization. Fix the declared input contract: example batch 3 contradicts min=6; either choose a valid example >=6 or a justified domain including 3, never suppress constraints. Define Dim ranges/relations, test boundary and second valid shapes plus deliberate invalid-shape rejection, ep.module comparison, save/load and target consumer. State strict mode explicitly (this pin defaults False) and respect installed API drift. A captured/exported graph proves no speedup. Separate cold compile/cache costs and repeated synchronized steady-state timings under equal state/shape/precision; service gains need separate L4 evidence.

## pytorch/sub-skills/memory-streams-and-graphs/allocator-race-and-replay

List allocation owner/aliases, producer and each consumer stream, last uses and completion. On consumer insert wait_stream(producer) before use; record_stream(consumer) or retain storage through completed use. record_stream controls reuse lifetime and does not order computation. Join worker back to original stream before consumption and synchronize relevant events/device before host observation. Host enqueue alone is not a safe release boundary. For graphs warm correct eager operations on a side stream, keep static input/output and graph references, copy new values into captured input storage in correct order, then replay and compare several changed values after completion. Rebinding the Python input points somewhere else and leaves the captured address unchanged. Measure allocated/reserved/peak and external device bytes at matching boundaries; live autograd/output references, cache and graph-private pools can retain memory. Reserved-minus-allocated is not proof of fragmentation, and empty_cache cannot free live/graph-owned storage or fix races. Tune one backend-appropriate allocator setting only after a bounded hypothesis.

## pytorch/sub-skills/distributed-and-checkpoint/dcp-trust-and-sharded-resume

Do not pass the received untrusted checkpoint to torch_save_to_dcp, DCP metadata/load or conversion. Establish provenance first; DCP conversion does not inherit weights_only protections and some readers explicitly use weights_only=False. Even explicit torch.load(weights_only=True) is restricted unpickling, not a hostile-input/resource sanitizer. For trusted job output recreate the target mesh and bottom-up fully_shard layers then root, allocate target state before DCP load, construct optimizer after sharding, and call model(x) to trigger hooks. Match rank membership/collective and state-key sequences. Restore model, optimizer/momentum, scheduler, scaler, RNG and sample progress, then compare a resumed update to uninterrupted control under the declared new sharding. Record local/global shapes and placements. For a hang preserve the first rank exception, compare device/group/order/shape/dtype sequence, then inspect readiness/network; do not just raise timeout. Complete or abort coherently and restart according to failure policy. Missing actual sharded/backend execution remains blocked.

## pytorch/sub-skills/profiling-and-debugging/trace-overhead-and-enqueue-time

The 20x number is unqualified because a CPU timer can measure CUDA enqueue. Fix workload/state/precision/thread/input boundary and correctness first. Use synchronized wall boundaries or timing events whose end event is synchronized; multi-stream dependencies must lie within the interval. Warm independently, measure replicates/distribution, and separate cold compile from steady state. For the diagnostic trace query supported_activities and actual CUPTI/device capability; a missing device event does not imply no device execution. Use a finite schedule with prof.step per step and check emitted artifacts/active interval. Begin with minimal CPU/device events and semantic record_function ranges; add shape/stack/memory options only for a specific question because they add overhead and retain tensors. Keep profiling runs separate from final timing. Report exact microbenchmark scope and unavailable device events, never a service gain without the frozen end-to-end evidence.

## pytorch/sub-skills/custom-operators-and-extension/fake-strides-versus-gradcheck

mutates_args=() means no input mutation; it does not permit the functional custom_op to return an input alias. Replace x.view_as(x) with a fresh output if that is the contract, or choose an explicitly supported alias/in-place/out schema and qualify its limitations. Define exact size/stride/storage_offset/dtype/device behavior; fake must match the real result using metadata only, so empty_like is valid only if its resulting layout matches. No data_ptr or value reads in fake. Keep traceable register_autograd/setup_context and save_for_backward. Incoming backward gradients can be noncontiguous: support their strides or deliberately materialize the required layout before the CUDA kernel. Run opcheck across dtype/device/stride/shape/requires_grad cases for registration, fake and functionalization; run double-precision gradcheck (and gradgradcheck if supported) separately for derivative math. Passing gradcheck cannot override opcheck failures. Compare eager/compile/export and actual CUDA stream/backend behavior only after contracts pass; CPU tests do not qualify CUDA.

## pytorch/integration/sharded-compiled-amp-resume

Freeze trusted checkpoint provenance, stack, mesh, tensor placement, data progress, RNG and eager reference. Recreate/shard bottom-up then root; construct optimizer from resulting parameters and load allocated model/optimizer/scheduler/scaler/RNG/sample-progress state. Use model(x), not forward directly. Loading weights alone omits momentum and sample state. Verify deterministic resumed forward/backward/parameter delta against uninterrupted control before compile. Shard IterableDataset across ranks/workers or use the proper sampler and set_epoch; check sample IDs, uneven shards and compatible per-rank collective counts rather than allowing one rank to silently exit early. Normalize microbatch loss over the actual effective window; unscale once after accumulation, clip once, step/update once and account for overflow/skipped scheduler advances. For the timeout locate the first rank error and diverging group/sequence/shape/dtype/device, then wait/abort coherently. Add Dynamo eager, aot_eager and actual compile separately, comparing gradients/state and inspecting guards; qualify actual FSDP2/compile/backend combinations. Performance work starts only after restart/update equivalence and collective correctness; hardware checks not run remain blocked.

## pytorch/integration/custom-attention-capture-export

Define attention Q/K/V shape/head/layout/dtype/device, mask semantics, causal policy and dropout; explicitly use dropout_p=0.0 for eval and compare with the eager math control. For the opaque custom op provide honest mutation/alias schema, a metadata-correct fake implementation without reading values, and traceable autograd where required. Check opcheck and gradcheck separately including noncontiguous/edge cases. CPU success establishes only that CPU contract. On actual CUDA compare forward/backward, current-stream behavior and dependencies before graphing. Capture warmed legal work with stable input/output storage; copy new values in place with proper ordering, replay changed inputs and preserve outputs before later reuse. Export the Module under explicit dynamic Dim bounds/strict choice, run ep.module on valid and invalid boundaries and test save/load. For ONNX use export-based dynamo=True/dynamic_shapes, choose a consumer-supported opset, verify custom-op translation/decomposition, package external-data weights, names/order and actual runtime dependencies, and compare target consumer outputs with tolerance. ONNX artifact generation alone does not prove target support. Keep CUDA, compiler and ONNX consumer execution as separate unresolved checks and measure only after correctness.

## torch-npu/root/novice-backend-and-routing

Start with installation-and-compatibility: choose one release matrix row or explicit source build line, recording torch/torch-npu, Python/Linux architecture, CANN, driver/firmware and hardware. Use a private environment and root inspect_environment.py for bounded package metadata; import and torch.npu registration do not prove device initialization. On the actual authorized NPU run inspect_environment.py --device for tiny allocation/matmul/completion and host result. Route missing registration to privateuse1-and-dispatch. Only after eager device correctness use graph-and-compile plus memory-streams-and-events for a selected manual/compiled route, stable input/output lifetime and updated-input replay. Then distributed-and-hccl for per-local-rank device setup and a bounded two-rank collective; add training-and-precision for AMP/state and profiling-and-debugging for trace questions. Without NPU, device kernels, allocator/capture, compiler target and HCCL checks remain BLOCKED_REQUIRED_BACKEND. Source/helper checks cannot establish those capabilities or speed/quality.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/installation-and-compatibility/release-versus-master

Do not reuse README commands as an interchangeable stack. The pinned release document includes 2.12 torch/torch-npu with CANN 9.1.0, while the source build lines are 2.13/2.14/2.15/2.16 and product 26.2/CANN9.2 rows are separate contexts. Choose to preserve the known released row, or build a distinct PyTorch2.14 development stack with its supported CANN/driver/hardware and Python ABI in an isolated disposable Linux environment. Source setup uses TORCH_VERSION or installed torch version stripped of local tag; version.txt alone does not choose the actual build. Record torch headers/ABI, exact source and gitlinks, optional TorchAir/FXRT/RPC feature flags. Initialize full build dependencies/submodules; do not run setup as a read-only query because metadata/codegen mutates files and copies/removes ACL working directories. Before touching the working environment inspect package versions and pip dependencies in the separate environment, then independently run import, device count, allocation, synchronized matmul and correct host result; compiler and HCCL remain further gates. No compatibility or backend result is claimed here.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/privateuse1-and-dispatch/lazy-import-contract

Use a fresh interpreter with the exact torch/torch-npu versions and autoload/import order recorded. Basic import loads core C-extension children then component registration, patches, lifecycle barrier and optional features, including op/custom/Meta registrations. PrivateUse1 is renamed npu, torch.npu and convenience methods are registered, but this registry phase must not initialize the device; npu._lazy_init owns runtime initialization. The pinned import test expects torch._dynamo, torch._inductor and torch_npu._inductor absent from sys.modules after only import torch_npu. Inspect their presence without importing them, and remove diagnostic imports that contaminate that boundary. Compare with a separately invoked torch.compile path, whose selected backend legitimately lazily initializes compiler modules. Do not infer a basic-import regression from a process that already compiled; preserve the first unexpected importer and version drift.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/operator-development/broadcast-custom-gradient

Define a namespaced schema with exact overload, dtype/device/layout, output size, mutation/alias/out constraints, broadcasting and gradient support. empty_like(self) is only correct for the extension example's narrow equal-shape contract; either reject broadcasting explicitly or infer broadcast result shape and promoted dtype for allocation and Meta. Register PrivateUse1 kernel separately from Meta/fake and autograd; the example uses AutogradPrivateUse1/AutogradMeta but those registrations do not prove derivative math. For broadcast Add reduce each incoming gradient to its original input shape instead of grad,grad. Respect device guard/current stream and retain wrapper checks; for built-in adaptation update owning YAML/schema and matching torchgen version then regenerate rather than patch outputs. Test metadata/schema first, then actual target NPU scalar/broadcast/noncontiguous/zero/invalid inputs, values and gradients, overlap/out rules, and compile/replay with updated values. Retain notices when adapting. No Meta or equal-shape eager result qualifies the full device/compiler matrix.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/memory-streams-and-events/record-stream-is-not-ordering

For x produced on A, enqueue B.wait_stream(A) before B uses x. While B uses it, x.record_stream(B) tells the allocator about lifetime; alternatively retain its storage until B completes. The wait itself does not retain Python ownership, and record_stream does not create a producer dependency. If A consumes B's result, A.wait_stream(B) must precede that use. Before reading asynchronously copied output on CPU or reporting timings, complete the relevant transfer/device stream; a host enqueue or event creation is insufficient. Keep externally pinned source owner alive and unmodified until nonblocking copy completion because foreign pointers may not be tracked by the pinned allocator. Return an ownership table of owner/aliases/allocating stream/using stream/wait edge/retention/completion, and compare allocated/active/reserved/host-pinned metrics at the same phase. Free-requested storage can remain event-pending and graph capture can defer reclamation. Use the tiny streams --run helper on real NPU; no cache reuse stress or device qualification follows from CPU inspection.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/graph-and-compile/eager-fallback-masquerade

Do not report compilation from this observation: at the inspected pin backend=npu uses TorchAir if present, otherwise can warn and return eager graph execution. Preserve the warning and actual selected compiler activity/build features. An eager fallback comparison cannot substantiate compiler speed. Distinguish manual NPUGraph fixed capture, backend=npugraphs built-in graph-tree setup, npugraph_ex optional package/config, backend=inductor with TORCHINDUCTOR_NPU_BACKEND selections and separate toolchains, and torch_npu.fxrt.backend optional inference runtime. None are automatic aliases or dependency installers. Select one supported route, establish eager NPU correctness, compare new input values/shapes/alias/mutation/output lifetime and record breaks/recompiles. Benchmark completed execution after warmup separately from capture/compile and keep target/backend checks blocked without the actual environment.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/distributed-and-hccl/future-versus-completion

The host future is marked complete in the launch path before HCCL end events; it is not a transfer-complete indication. Producers are ordered onto communication streams, but lifetime requires record-stream tracking or the configured retained-reference path. Keep inputs/outputs alive through actual work. Work.wait orders the current consumer stream on the HCCL end event and only host-blocks in configured modes; an unrelated consumer stream needs its own event/wait edge. Synchronize the relevant device/stream after waiting before host reads, buffer reuse or elapsed-time claims. Run torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=2 <SKILL_ROOT>/scripts/runtime_smoke.py --case hccl --run on two assigned NPUs with matching stack. Select LOCAL_RANK before group init, finite timeout, same collective sequence and tiny rank-dependent tensor; all_reduce, wait, synchronize, verify expected sum, coherently destroy group. This checks only that local collective, not fabric/scaling/overlap/service performance. Missing devices leave HCCL blocked.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/training-and-precision/accumulation-clipping

Establish tiny FP32 eager reference and save initial model/optimizer/RNG. Clear gradients once for the effective batch; for four microbatches normalize each loss by four and scale/backward with unchanged scale, backward outside autocast. After all four call unscale_(optimizer) once, clip unscaled gradients once, scaler.step then scaler.update once. Normalize a shorter final window by its actual size. Do not mix scaled and unscaled gradients or update scale during accumulation. Observe scaler.is_enabled, per-optimizer state, nonfinite/device overflow, scale before/after, skipped step and actual parameter delta; disabled scaler on the test host is not AMP validation. Compare loss/gradients/update against chosen-tolerance FP32 on the actual NPU and supported dtype, including overflow/skipped-update behavior and state restore. Windows CPU leaves NPU AMP BLOCKED_REQUIRED_BACKEND, not passed; one step does not prove convergence.

## torch-npu/sub-skills/profiling-and-debugging/empty-timeline-async-parse

profile_memory alone does not satisfy timeline prerequisites: set record_shapes=True, profile_memory=True and with_stack=True or with_modules=True. Pick CPU/NPU activities supported by the actual profiling runtime, finite wait/warmup/active/repeat and enough iterations, advancing prof.step each intended step. Inspect effective schedule/warnings and actual active artifacts, then synchronize at the intended workload completion boundary. Record collection, parsing, archive and viewer status separately. Async parsing can fail even after trace directory creation; await analysis futures and retain original data/error, rather than declaring a usable timeline from a nonempty path. Inspect CANN profiling capability and required runtime/debug dependencies on the target. Re-run a minimal correct workload with necessary options; profiling changes overhead and lifetime, so keep final timings separate. No NPU trace capability is established on a CPU host.

## torch-npu/integration/updated-input-fork-join

Qualify eager two-stream correctness first. Main-stream producers must precede the expert consumer through wait/event edges; capture the fork and join back to main before dependent output and before ending the intended capture. Record cross-stream uses or retain storage separately from ordering. Use a legal non-default managed capture stream, with compatible task-queue/pinned allocator configuration. Keep graph, pool and static input/output storage alive. Copy updated values into each captured branch input address, ordering copies before replay; changing a Python variable only updates that variable. Compare both branches against eager on several changed inputs after completion. Replay may reuse captured output storage; clone/copy any output that must survive the next replay. del can lower allocated bytes while pending events, caches and graph/private-pool references keep storage reserved, and capture defers reclamation; inspect all owners and matching completion-phase metrics before any allocator tuning. Do not force cache clearing or infer a leak from reserved bytes. Time only after correct joins, output retention and updated-input checks, on the actual NPU.

## torch-npu/integration/hccl-amp-trace-state

Keep three state machines separate. HCCL host future completion precedes device end-event completion; Work.wait orders the current stream, so synchronize/establish consumer edges and retain buffers before host reads/reuse. For the scaler inspect enabled state, per-optimizer scaled/unscaled/stepped state, finite gradients/device and distributed overflow, scale before/after and actual parameter mutation. An overflow-skipped update may be correct; unscale/clip once after the full accumulation window and update once per optimizer boundary, preserving sharded placements/group identities. For profiler inspect supported CPU/NPU activities, actual CANN collection, schedule active interval and prof.step, requested memory shape/stack-or-module options, then parsing futures and usable events; directory creation is not trace success. Validate each subsystem separately before composing the sharded job, retaining first rank errors/sequence differences and exact stack. A Windows CPU host can inspect helpers/contracts and CPU controls only; NPU AMP/HCCL/device trace and sharded integration remain BLOCKED_REQUIRED_BACKEND, and performance/convergence remain not_run.
